---
title: "Theme"
---

## Enabling the theme

```python
import attaviz
attaviz.enable()                  # medium size (default)
attaviz.enable(size="small")      # charts under ~400px wide
attaviz.enable(size="large")      # charts wider than ~700px
```

`enable()` registers and activates a theme variant globally. Every subsequent Altair chart in the session picks up WBG typography, colors, grids, and mark styling.

## What the theme applies

| Element | WBG specification |
|---|---|
| Font | Open Sans, sans-serif |
| Title | 18px, bold, `#111111` |
| Subtitle | 15px, regular, `#666666` |
| Axis labels | 13px, semibold, `#111111` |
| Tick labels | 13px, regular, `#666666` |
| Grid lines | `#CED4DE`, 1px, dashed (4 2) |
| Legend | 14×14px symbol dots, semibold labels |
| Categorical colors | 9-color WBG palette |
| Sequential colors | WBG blue ramp (default) |
| Diverging colors | WBG default diverging scale |
| Line marks | 4px stroke, round caps/joins |
| Point marks | 1px white stroke outline |
| Geo shapes | 0.3px grey stroke, round joins |

The values above are the `medium` defaults. `small` and `large` scale typography and spacing proportionally.

## Size system

| Size | Typical width | Typography / spacing |
|---|---|---|
| `small` | under 400px | compact |
| `medium` | 400–700px | default |
| `large` | over 700px | expanded |

Registered names: `wbg` (the default medium size), `wbg-small`, `wbg-medium`, and `wbg-large`.

## Per-chart sizing

```{python}
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
import attaviz

attaviz.enable()
data = pd.DataFrame({"category": ["A", "B", "C"], "value": [10, 25, 18]})
chart = attaviz.bar(data, category="category", value="value", title="Example values")
attaviz.configure_size(chart, width=600, aspect_ratio="16:9")
```

`configure_size()` adds top-level Altair configuration for a standalone chart.
For a chart you will pass to `frame()`, specify `width` and `height` on the
template and choose typography with `enable(size=...)`; Altair cannot nest a
configured chart inside another composition.

- `width` — target pixel width; the size variant is inferred automatically.
- `height` — optional explicit pixel height, overriding the aspect ratio.
- `aspect_ratio` — `"1:1"`, `"4:3"`, `"3:2"`, `"16:9"`, `"2:1"`, `"square"`,
  `"widescreen"`, or a numeric width/height ratio such as `1.5`.

## Calculating dimensions

```{python}
w, h = attaviz.calculate_dimensions(800, "16:9")  # (800, 450)
attaviz.bar(data, category="category", value="value", width=w, height=h)
```

Useful when you need the height up front (e.g. for a faceted chart whose rows must add up to a known total).

## Size context managers

To override the active theme for a single chart (or a block of charts) without changing the global setting, use `alt.theme.enable` as a context manager against the registered variants:

```{python}
theme_registry = alt.theme if hasattr(alt, "theme") else alt.themes

with theme_registry.enable("wbg-small"):
    small_chart = attaviz.bar(data, category="category", value="value", width=300, height=150)
    small_chart.to_dict()  # serialize/export while the temporary theme is active

with theme_registry.enable("wbg-large"):
    large_chart = attaviz.bar(data, category="category", value="value", width=800, height=400)
    large_chart.to_dict()
```

`alt.theme` is the current Altair interface; the fallback keeps this example compatible with older supported Altair 5 releases. When the block exits, the previously active theme is restored. Altair applies the theme when serializing the chart, so display or export inside the block to capture that temporary theme.

## Theme configuration

`wbg_theme()` returns the raw theme dictionary. Use `size`, `width`, `height`, and `aspect_ratio` to inspect or register a configuration for a specific output medium:

```{python}
@alt.theme.register("wbg-widescreen", enable=True)
def wbg_widescreen():
    return alt.theme.ThemeConfig(
        attaviz.wbg_theme(width=1200, aspect_ratio="16:9")
    )

chart = attaviz.bar(data, category="category", value="value", width=1200, height=675)
chart.to_dict()  # includes the custom theme configuration
attaviz.enable()  # restore the default for subsequent examples
```

Typography and spacing scale off the supplied `width` using the size breakpoints above (so a 1200px theme inherits `large` tokens).

This registration example uses the current registry introduced in Altair 5.5. On older Altair 5 releases, register a function returning the raw `wbg_theme()` dictionary through `alt.themes.register()`, then enable it with `alt.themes.enable()`.

## Sizing constants

For custom theming or introspection, these constants are re-exported:

- `attaviz.SIZE_BREAKPOINTS` — `{"small": 400, "medium": 700}`
- `attaviz.TYPOGRAPHY` — per-size font-size dicts
- `attaviz.SPACING` — per-size spacing tokens (`xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`)
- `attaviz.ASPECT_RATIOS` — named ratio lookup
- `attaviz.DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS` — default `(w, h)` per size
